title: Sparse-KV adaptive memory profiling for extended-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Emily Chen
description: Goal: Design and validate a model-specific 'sparse-KV' memory profile layer that adaptively trades GPU residency vs host offload and eviction aggressiveness for Llama, Mistral, and Qwen variants when serving extended-context (>=32k) workloads with continuous batching. This ticket covers benchmarking, heuristics, implementation knobs (slice granularity, hotset window, eviction score), and rollout plan across hosted and Dedicated clusters. The profile should reduce peak GPU memory by at least 25% for tail long-context sequences while keeping median token latency within SLOs and avoiding quality regressions due to premature KV eviction. Deliverables: (1) spec for sparse-KV residency policy and profile generator, (2) benchmark harness & dashboards, (3) runtime flag + rollout gated by perf/regression checks, (4) migration guide for Dedicated GPU pools.
comments: 2026-03-10 | Emily Chen: Kickoff notes: we observed repeated OOMs on Dedicated rtx-a5000 pools when serving qwen-32k with mixed batching (continuous batching enabled). Initial profiling shows KV residency accounts for ~42% of peak allocation for 32k sequences. Proposed approach: instead of uniform KV residency we compute per-layer hotness and create sparse residency masks + a tiered eviction score (recency * layer-weight * token-density).

2026-03-11 | Raj Patel: Ran first round of microbenchmarks comparing three strategies on Llama-70B-32k: (A) baseline full-residency, (B) coarse slice-offload (8-layer granularity), (C) sparse-KV with per-layer hotset (adaptive). Results: (B) reduced peak memory by 18% but increased p95 token latency by 12% due to offload jitter. (C) reduced peak by 27% with p95 latency +4% — promising tradeoff. Collected traces and heap dumps uploaded to: https://drive.redwood/internal/bench/sparse-kv/2026-03-11

2026-03-12 | Sofia Martinez: Design review: reviewed sparse residency mask schema. Feedback: make mask generation deterministic per model+token-window seed, expose 'hotset_alpha' and 'slice_granularity' as runtime knobs, and add metrics for eviction_count_by_layer and offload_io_ms. Also recommend adding per-variant defaults: llama-70b: alpha=0.85,slice=4; mistral-30b: alpha=0.9,slice=6; qwen-32b: alpha=0.78,slice=3.

2026-03-12 | Raj Patel: Implemented profile generator prototype in runtime/profiles/sparse_kv.py (branch: feat/sparse-kv-profiles). Hooked generator into serving startup path when model.manifest has 'sparse_kv: true'. Added config to console to preview predicted memory curve. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4587

2026-03-13 | Ops (Alex Nguyen): Smoke on Dedicated: deployed branch to canary pool (gpu-dedicated-canary-2). Observed that background offload IO spikes correlate with throughput peaks — need to rate-limit offload IO and add jitter to eviction to avoid synchronized IO storms. Plan: add offload backpressure that reduces batching window when offload queue > threshold.

2026-03-13 | Raj Patel: Updated benchmark run with offload IO backpressure enabled. For Qwen-32k bursts with continuous batching target 200 rps: peak GPU mem down 29%, p95 latency up 6% but under p95 SLO. Will run cross-variant regression suite overnight.
